# mcp_registry Usage Guide

<!-- socrates:section id="purpose" kind="purpose" tags="tools" -->
## Purpose

- `mcp_registry`: Discover, validate, add, or delete Model Context Protocol servers. When a user asks for a helper, extension, server, integration, or custom capability, use list then describe with the canonical id. When the user explicitly asks to add a server and provides its trusted command/config, configure saves it disabled, checks the handshake/tools, and enables only on success. Declare required secret key names in secretBindings; never read, request, infer, or provide secret values yourself. Use source=workspace_env only when the user explicitly asked to reuse that exact key from a workspace .env file; otherwise use source=user_input so Socrates can collect it privately. Use delete only after an explicit user request. Do not invent packages, commands, URLs, or credentials.
<!-- /socrates:section -->

<!-- socrates:section id="when_to_use" kind="routing" tags="tools" -->
## When To Use

- Use `mcp_registry` when the active task requires its cataloged mutation/execution capability.
<!-- /socrates:section -->

<!-- socrates:section id="inputs" kind="schema" tags="tools" -->

- `mcp_registry` uses the one canonical schema owned by `tool.mcp_registry`; send only documented fields and do not add aliases or placeholder values.

- If input validation fails, correct the call against the canonical schema; do not guess, normalize, or silently drop fields.
